chunks: Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn al-Yasaʿ narrated from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Mihran, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a woman into whose home a thief entered while she was pregnant, and he assaulted her and killed what was in her womb. Then the woman sprang upon the thief and killed him. He said: “As for the woman who killed him, there is nothing upon her, and the diyyah for her unborn child is upon the ʿaṣabah of the slain thief.”

key_terms.دِيَةُ سَخْلَتِهَا: the blood money for her unborn child
key_terms.عَصَبَةِ الْمَقْتُولِ السَّارِقِ: the agnatic male relatives of the slain thief who bear the compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pregnant woman kills a thief who assaulted her and caused the death of her unborn child?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a pregnant woman who was assaulted by a thief, resulting in the death of the child in her womb, after which she killed the attacker. The Imam عليه السلام rules that no liability falls upon the woman for killing him, while the blood money for the unborn child is owed by the male agnatic relatives of the slain thief. The narration addresses criminal injury, self-defense, and compensation for fetal death.
